transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 16:00 PST 
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (LumenBio VP Eng), Diego Marquez (LumenBio SRE), Nora Chen (LumenBio ML Eng)

Auto Notes / Quick summary: Weekly POC sync. Focus: throughput/profile adjustments, reduce tail latency spikes during bursty traffic, tune continuous batching and concurrency targets, confirm next stress runs and deliverables.

---

[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we put this at 30 minutes, looks like we have a bit more time, so great. quick roll call?
[00:22] Aisha: Aisha here, Diego, Nora are with me. morning everyone.
[00:34] Morgan: great. priya and samir from my side. priya you wanna lead the run review?
[00:45] Priya: yeah, thanks. i'll pull up the week three runs. so we executed the steady-state 300 qps and a burst test at ~900 qps for 10 minutes, same model variant you sent (lumenb-v2-quant). results are in the sheet i posted — link in chat — and overall throughput improved with continuous batching at window 24ms but we saw tail latency spikes at 95th and 99th percentiles during ramp down.
[01:18] Nora: just to be clear, that ramp down spike was the one where requests queued up and then flooded the model? we saw a few 2-3x latencies, yes.
[01:32] Priya: exact. what happened is the queue depth built while the concurrency cap prevented more inflight, then when KV cache warmed, a bunch of requests hit long context writes and caused the long tail.
[01:48] Diego: hmm we saw similar in our logs. the SRE team thinks the client-side retry backoff isn't smoothing enough, we have a bit of synchronized retry.
[02:02] Morgan: okay so multiple contributing factors: batching window, concurrency cap, retry behavior, and cache warmup. any immediate blockers to adjusting the batching window?
[02:15] Aisha: cost is a factor — if you bump the window too much we get higher token spend. we need target latency under 250ms p95 for product launch.
[02:26] Priya: understood. our proposal: two parallel knobs — first, soften the batching window from 24ms to 18ms but add an adaptive window step that expands to 36ms if queue depth > X. second, enforce a sliding concurrency cap per worker to avoid thundering when cache warms. this should lower p99 spikes without raising steady-state cost too much.
[02:50] Nora: can you explain adaptive window briefly? like how that threshold is computed?
[02:56] Priya: yep — we use a moving average of queue depth over 1s; if it exceeds the target (we suggest 40 requests), the engine increases the batching window by 1.5x up to 36ms. that gives us better packing during bursts. the risk is slightly higher per-token latency for single requests, but tail latency improves.
[03:22] Diego: what's the concurrency cap you recommend?
[03:27] Priya: start with 8 inflight per shard for your workload. we saw 8-ish gives good throughput/lower latency; your current was 20 which is why queueing built.
[03:37] Aisha: 8 seems low — will that throttle steady throughput too much?
[03:42] Priya: we pair concurrency with burst capacity — when CPU/GPU util is low we allow short-lived bursts to 16 via burst tokens, so average is stable but we don't let unlimited concurrency during warmup.
[03:58] Morgan: another lever is prefix/KV cache warmup. we attached a simple warmup script in the runbook that hits frequent prefixes to prime the KV. did you try it?
[04:10] Nora: we ran a small warmup but not like the script — ours targeted single prefixes. we'll try the full warmup.
[04:17] Diego: note — our environment has node auto-scaling that sometimes spins up new workers, that resets cache. we need guidance on warmup for ephemeral nodes.
[04:30] Priya: good call. we'll add an init-hook warmup and a short period of auto-warm before sending production traffic. should be~60-90s.

[04:52] Speaker 1: couple quick micro notes from logs — during one of the bursts, there was a model fallback event to a quantized variant that increased latency, maybe due to nodal OOMs, that could be an unrelated factor.

[05:10] Morgan: thanks. ok the plan we sketched: adjust window/adaptive step, set concurrency cap to 8 with burst token to 16, add warmup hook, and tweak client retry backoff. any objections?
[05:28] Aisha: no objections, just need to see the cost delta.
[05:33] Priya: we'll compute an estimated cost delta and post into the benchmark sheet — rough estimate tonight.

[05:46] Diego: another item — queueing instrumentation. right now our dashboards show tokens and latency but not a clear per-shard queue depth; can redwood expose per-shard queue depth metric?
[05:59] Priya: yes we can surface queue_depth.{shard_id} and a derived metric queue_saturation. i'll add it to the telemetry namespace and add a Grafana panel template.
[06:12] Nora: perfect, that will help us correlate spikes with node events.

[06:24] Samir: quick note on the SLA side — you mentioned needing p95 < 250ms. for pilot we can set that as a goal; if we enter Dedicated later we can set SLOs tied to reserved capacity.
[06:39] Aisha: sounds good. timeline question — how fast can we iterate on the suggested knobs?
[06:44] Priya: we can push the engine changes to your reserved trial cluster within 24 hours; then we need one full burst run (10–15m) and a steady 1hr run to validate. so rough 48–72h to get a reliable read.
[07:00] Diego: ok we'll schedule the burst tomorrow morning. who will own the script changes?
[07:06] Priya: i'll own the runbook edits and the telemetry panel. Morgan will schedule the canary demo.

[07:18] Morgan: noted. also want to discuss fallback policies — we had one failed with fallback to a lower-quality variant which increased latency unexpectedly. priya?
[07:30] Priya: yeah fallback is currently configured to route to quantized-compat models when out-of-memory or other hardware errors occur. we should change policy to prefer regional fallback or serve a short error with retry, rather than automatically switching to a slower variant. that'll reduce surprise tail latencies.
[07:50] Nora: do you have a config suggestion?
[07:53] Priya: switch to: primary -> regional primary replica -> short 503 with Retry-After header; only fallback to model variant if error_rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes. that'll keep latency profile stable.
[08:09] Aisha: ok that seems sensible.

[08:18] [08:18] Morgan: can we also add a canary policy demo next week so we can see behavior live?
[08:24] Aisha: yes please.

[08:30] Priya: final bit: we captured a small bug in the client's retry jitter calculation where jitter was too small (0.2s) — increase to randomized 0.5-1.2s window to avoid synchronized retries.
[08:45] Diego: we'll patch that on our side.

[08:52] Morgan: awesome. recap and owners: priya updates runbook+telemetry, diego runs bursty stress and uploads logs, nora validates warmup, morgan schedules canary demo. we'll target follow-up next week same time.

[09:12] Aisha: thanks everyone. any privacy/security notes? we did ask earlier about logs — need assurances on audit logs and PII scrubbing.
[09:25] Samir: short answer — for pilot we use pseudonymized logs; full private deployment includes KMS/HSM integrations and SOC2 docs which we can share. i'll send the security packet after the call.

[09:40] Nora: one last question — do you have a recommended steady-state concurrency target per CPU/GPU? we are on A100 style nodes.
[09:50] Priya: for A100-ish and quantized LLMs we recommend 6-12 inflight depending on sequence length; for your median sequence length we saw 8 is sweet spot. we'll add a quick reference table to the runbook.

[10:08] Morgan: perfect. ok thanks all. we'll follow-up with the links and schedule.
